title: factdiff.py detect run twice in one day overwrites the tracked detect log of that day
goal: factdiff.py detect writes a new log name (or appends) when the day's detect log already exists in the root's census directory, so a second detect run in one day never replaces a committed log

run:
import sys, os, tempfile, argparse, collections
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import factdiff as f, provider, kbcommon
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
f.root_path = lambda rel: os.path.join(t, rel)
f.sources = lambda: {}
f.cited_facts = lambda prefix=None: {}
f.read_anchors = lambda: {}
f.read_state = lambda: {}
f.write_state = lambda s: None
f.select_ids = lambda a, s: []
provider.providers = lambda r: []
log = f.root_path(os.path.join(kbcommon.CENSUS_DIR, "factdiff-2026-01-01.csv"))
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(log))
open(log, "w").write("SENTINEL committed log\n")
a = argparse.Namespace(date="2026-01-01", out=None, sitemaps=False, no_save=False, topic=[], dir=[], file=[], source=[])
f.cmd_detect(a, collections.Counter())
kept = "SENTINEL" in open(log).read()
print("committed log kept:", kept)
sys.exit(0 if kept else 1)

clauses.clause: factdiff.py detect writes a new log name (or appends) when the day's detect log already exists in the root's census directory, so a second detect run in one day never replaces a committed log

gates.question: How does detect avoid replacing the day's existing log?
options: append rows to the existing log
gates.reason: appended rows would double-process a source in apply and review

notes: Found 2026-11-09 when a refresh run had to restore the tracked log after a second detect overwrote it. Premise: the repro (cmd_detect in process on a planted root holding a committed same-day log) exits 1 on 55dde769f: the log is rewritten.
